reword.careplan.early_visit.title: Your first visit after birth
reword.careplan.early_visit.body: See your practice in the first three weeks after birth. The clinician checks how you are healing and answers your questions. Bring your questions and a list of your medicines. If you need a ride or an interpreter, tell the practice first.
reword.careplan.comprehensive_visit.title: Your six-week visit
reword.careplan.comprehensive_visit.body: A full visit about six weeks after birth. It covers how you are healing, your mood, birth control if you want it, and what comes next. Bring your questions, your medicine list, and your insurance card. Ask about anything still open.
reword.careplan.mood_checkin_explained.title: The mood questions, explained
reword.careplan.mood_checkin_explained.body: Around day 14 you get a short set of mood questions. It is a standard set your care team uses. It is not a diagnosis. You choose who sees the answers, and you can skip it. A clinician reviews the answers and may call you.
reword.careplan.feeding_support.title: Help with feeding
reword.careplan.feeding_support.body: However you feed your baby, help is there if it is hard. Your practice can connect you with feeding support in the first week. Sore nipples, low supply, or bottle trouble are all good reasons to ask. Tell your coordinator.
reword.careplan.newborn_visit.title: Your baby's first visit
reword.careplan.newborn_visit.body: Your baby's first visit with a pediatric clinician is usually in the first week. It is separate from your own visit. No pediatric clinician yet? Tell your coordinator. If getting there is hard, say so and the practice will help.
reword.careplan.pelvic_floor_recovery.title: Healing your pelvic floor
reword.careplan.pelvic_floor_recovery.body: The muscles that hold up your bladder and bowel take time to recover. Leaking urine, pain, or pressure are common and worth raising. Your clinician can talk about exercises or a referral to pelvic floor therapy. Ask at your six-week visit or sooner.
reword.careplan.contraception_conversation.body: If you want it, your clinician will talk about birth control at your six-week visit. You can bring it up earlier. There are many options, and the choice is yours. Bring your questions.
reword.careplan.blood_pressure_check.title: Checking your blood pressure
reword.careplan.blood_pressure_check.body: If your clinician asked you to check your blood pressure, do it in the first week. Your practice tells you when and how. A bad headache, vision changes, or swelling of your face or hands mean call right away.
reword.careplan.transition_primary_care.title: Moving to your regular clinician
reword.careplan.transition_primary_care.body: At twelve weeks your care moves to your primary care clinician. The practice confirms who that is and what is still open. No primary care clinician yet? Tell your coordinator so one can be found.
reword.careplan.mental_health_connection.title: Connecting with mental health support
reword.careplan.mental_health_connection.body: If you and your clinician agree more support would help, the practice can refer you to a mental health partner. The practice tracks the referral until an appointment has happened. Ask any time. If you cannot wait, call or text 988.
